claims.text: Heating the additive-manufacturing build chamber to 500–600 °C will reduce thermal gradients during solidification of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients will diminish compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
A heated build chamber will decrease residual stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
A heated build chamber will reduce defect formation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect formation will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to ambient-chamber additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention is substrate preheating in a build chamber maintained at 500–600 °C.
Heated-chamber processing will produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Heated-chamber processing will lower porosity in AlCrFeNiSi.
Heated-chamber processing will diminish dislocation density in AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating accelerates heat dissipation uniformly through the deposited material.
Preheating produces a slower and more controlled cooling rate.
Slower, controlled cooling minimizes solute redistribution during solidification.
Slower, controlled cooling minimizes internal stress buildup during solidification.
Heated-chamber specimens will exhibit a more uniform elemental distribution than ambient-chamber specimens.
Heated-chamber specimens will have lower XRD-measured residual thermal stress than ambient-chamber specimens.
Heated-chamber specimens may have 15–25% higher tensile strength and ductility than ambient-chamber specimens.
Ambient-chamber additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically causes faster cooling than heated-chamber processing.
Ambient-chamber additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces greater segregation and higher residual stress.
The expected benefits are limited to additive manufacturing with other process parameters held constant and chamber temperature controlled within 500–600 °C.
Elevated chamber temperatures may create oxidation problems that could adversely affect the material.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says preheating both accelerates heat dissipation and produces slower cooling. These statements are in tension unless the intended distinction between heat-flow uniformity and net cooling rate is explained.
